frontmatter.title: The Enough Question
frontmatter.statement: How much money would it take to fix a specific problem at its source, and is it true that money isn’t the bottleneck?
frontmatter.progress: Costed source-level plans for specific problems, judged by independent experts, and a record of what happened when such plans were funded.
frontmatter.bounty: Unfunded. The Question Bounties program will attach prizes once it is funded.

subject.body:
## Why it matters

Humanity’s Checklist points out that hundreds of billions of dollars go to charity every year, and asks what would happen if $5 million, spent correctly, were enough to go after the six sources upstream of every world problem. Charitology treats that as a hypothesis to test, not a slogan. If money really isn’t the bottleneck, the field should find out what is.

## Where to start

Pick one problem, write the source-level plan, cost it, fund it and publish what happens, including if it fails.
